title: Automation Engineer Roadmap
summary: Build from instrumentation and control fundamentals into PLC/SCADA, industrial networks, DCS, robotics, process control and industrial automation systems.

facts.Timeline assumption: Four-year B.Tech/B.E. beginning in 2026 and completing around 2030. Each semester should produce a practical automation, instrumentation or control deliverable.

about.label: Career fit
about.text: Automation Engineer is a directly aligned career path for Electronics & Instrumentation Engineering;

horizons.question: What can I enter now?
horizons.output: build instrumentation, control, PLC, SCADA, industrial networking and troubleshooting skills.

horizons.question: How should I specialise?
horizons.output: specialise in PLC/SCADA, DCS/process automation, robotics, industrial IoT or motion control.

horizons.question: How should I evolve?
horizons.output: progress toward senior automation, controls, commissioning, systems integration or project engineering.

horizons.question: How can I remain relevant?
horizons.output: combine automation with industrial cybersecurity, IIoT, digital twins, AI-assisted control and data-driven operations.

blocks.label: Evolve and stay relevant, 2035–2046
blocks.text: Automation engineering is expanding from isolated PLC programming toward connected operational technology. Develop skills across controls, networking, data, cybersecurity, robotics and industrial software rather than depending on a single PLC vendor.

blocks.label: Career progression

blocks.text: PhD routes

Maintain strong control and instrumentation fundamentals while expanding into industrial cybersecurity, IIoT, robotics, digital twins, edge computing and AI-assisted process optimisation. The strongest long-term foundation is the ability to understand both the physical process and the software controlling it.
